title: Pricing change notice and revenue reconciliation procedure
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This procedure defines the cross-functional steps required when changing pricing or billing terms for Redwood Inference customers, and the downstream revenue recognition (RevRec) and forecasting adjustments required. The goal is to: (1) ensure consistent legal and procurement approvals; (2) provide deterministic notification timelines to customers and internal teams; (3) produce auditable RevRec adjustments and journal entries; (4) update FP&A forecasts and committed capacity accounting.

Scope:
- Applies to all changes that modify customer-facing pricing, billing cadence, or contract charge quantities: rate card changes, discounts, credits, one-time fees, term amendments, capacity commits, and early termination fees.
- Exclusions: purely marketing price lists that do not change existing contracts, internal list-price experiments (<72 hours) with no customer impact.

Key definitions:
- Pricing Change: any modification to the monetary terms in an executed agreement or an active billing relationship.
- Amendment Effective Date: the date the new pricing/billing terms take legal effect.
- Billing Cutoff Date: final invoice date using old pricing.
- RevRec Adjustment Window: 90 days post-amendment for accounting adjustments and catch-up.

Owners and responsibilities (high level):
- Sales: initiates pricing change request, completes commercial justification.
- Legal: drafts amendment and approves final contract language.
- Procurement (customer side): confirms customer acceptance and PO alignment (if applicable).
- Finance (Revenue Operations / RevRec): validates accounting treatment, prepares journal entries, issues billing adjustments.
- FP&A: updates forecasts and model assumptions.
- Billing/Payments (Finance Ops): executes invoices/credit memos and updates billing system.
- Customer Success: communicates operational impact and coordinates customer acceptance.

Notice triggers and SLAs:
1) Internal approval target: all pricing changes must have commercial, legal, and finance approval 10 business days before Amendment Effective Date.
2) Customer-facing notice: standard notice is 30 days prior to Amendment Effective Date for recurring price increases or structural changes.
3) Emergency/expedited changes: approval window can be shortened to 3 business days with Executive sponsor approval; Finance must manually validate RevRec impact before go-live.

Pre-change checklist (Sales lead):
- Confirm product/sku mapping for affected charges.
- Provide expected billing delta by customer (monthly run rate delta).
- Confirm if change affects committed capacity or reserved billing.
- Attach customer PO or email acceptance (if required).
- Select Amendment Effective Date and propose Billing Cutoff Date.

Approval workflow (step-by-step):
1) Sales uploads Pricing Change Request (PCR) into Contract Intake Workspace (Confluence template link) containing: customer, contract id, old/new rates, effective dates, reason, revenue owner, and estimated MRR/ARR impact.
2) Legal reviews draft amendment and flags any non-standard clauses.
3) Finance (RevRec) assesses accounting treatment and flags any immediate revenue deferral or acceleration needs.
4) Procurement or Customer Success obtains formal customer acceptance signature or PO.
5) Final sign-off recorded in the PCR and the amendment executed.

Billing execution and RevRec steps after amendment effective date:
1) Billing/Payments: generate invoice run using new rates on or after Billing Cutoff Date. Issue any automated proration rules per billing system policy.
2) RevRec (Revenue Operations): calculate the revenue impact by identifying the overlap period where the old rate was previously recognized and the new rate applies.
3) If a retrospective correction is required (e.g., retrospective credit or back-billed invoice), Finance must: a) prepare credit memos or invoices, b) record corresponding journal entries, and c) document rationale in the PCR.

Accounting treatment guidance (common scenarios):
- Simple recurring price increase (prospective): Recognize revenue per normal schedule; adjust future forecasts. No retrospective RevRec entry required if amendment is prospective.
- Mid-term rate change with retroactive billing (customer approved back-billing): Recognize additional revenue when invoiced; if payment expected after period end, record receivable and assess collectibility. Consider ASC 606 guidance on contract modifications.
- One-time credits or refunds: Issue credit memo and reduce recognized revenue in the RevRec Adjustment Window. Document control: link credit memo to amendment id.

Sample journal entries (illustrative):
- Prospective increase (no retro): No adjustment to historical entries.
- Retroactive billing issued for Jan-Mar period and invoiced in May:
  Debit: Accounts Receivable $30,000
  Credit: Revenue (prior periods catch-up) $28,000
  Credit: Deferred Tax/Other adjustments $2,000  (if tax or timing)
- Issuing customer credit for overbilling:
  Debit: Revenue Reduction/Contra-Revenue $5,000
  Credit: Accounts Receivable or Cash $5,000

Forecasting & FP&A alignment:
- FP&A must update recurring revenue models within 5 business days of amendment execution. Updates include: monthly run-rate, churn adjustments, committed capacity revenue schedules, and GAAP vs. cash waterfall.
- For material amendments (>5% of ARR per customer or >$250k ARR delta), FP&A and RevOps must produce a reconciliation memo and present in the next Finance weekly forecast review.

Reporting and reconciliation controls (monthly cadence):
- Revenue Operations runs the Pricing Change Reconciliation report (PCRR) each month which includes: list of amendments executed, effective dates, invoiced deltas, outstanding credit memos, and pending disputes.
- Reconciliation queries (example SQL-like pseudo-query):
  SELECT contract_id, amendment_id, effective_date, sum(new_amount - old_amount) as monthly_delta
  FROM billing_events
  WHERE effective_date BETWEEN :start_date AND :end_date
  GROUP BY contract_id, amendment_id

- Automation: Revenue Ops maintains a mapping table of amendment ids to invoice ids used in automated reconciliation scripts. Exceptions feed a ticket to RevRec for manual review.

Customer communication templates (condensed):
- Price increase notification subject: "Notice: Updates to your Redwood Inference pricing effective [DATE]"
- Template bullet points to include: brief rationale, affected SKUs, Amendment Effective Date, Billing Cutoff Date, contact for questions, link to amendment document, and instructions for PO updates.

Escalation matrix:
- Day 0–5 post-amendment: Billing/Payments handles invoice issuance and straightforward disputes.
- Day 6–30: RevRec and Sales resolve pricing discrepancies and approve credit memos.
- >30 days: Escalate to Head of Finance and General Counsel for disputed legacy billing beyond standard Credit Policy window.

Controls, audit trail and evidence retention:
- All pricing changes must be stored in Contract Intake Workspace and linked to: executed amendment PDF, PCR ticket, customer acceptance artifact, and invoice/credit memo ids.
- Retain evidence for 7 years for audit purposes per company policy.

Templates and artifacts (links and examples):
- PCR Confluence template: [link to template]
- Amendment checklist (embedded): 1) commercial summary, 2) legal clause exceptions, 3) RevRec sign-off, 4) invoices to be reissued, 5) communications log.
- Sample credit memo JSON (billing system snippet):
  {
    "customer_id": "CUST-12345",
    "amendment_id": "AMEND-2026-004",
    "amount": "-5000.00",
    "currency": "USD",
    "reason_code": "PRICE_CORRECT"
  }

Operational notes and best practices:
- If a pricing change triggers a change in committed capacity, coordinate with Infrastructure Finance to update committed GPU reservation invoicing and capacity reporting.
- Apply rounding and proration rules consistently: default to bill on a per-day proration basis for mid-cycle changes unless customer requests otherwise.
- Where possible, prefer prospective amendments to avoid complex retroactive accounting and customer disputes.

KPIs and monitoring:
- Time-to-approval (goal: <10 business days)
- % of pricing changes requiring retrospective correction (goal: <5%)
- Average time to clear pricing disputes (goal: <15 business days)
- Forecast delta accuracy after pricing changes (goal: <2% variance reported vs. revised forecast)

Appendix A — Example calculation:
- Customer A had $100k monthly at old rate. On 2026-03-01 rate increased to $110k monthly. Amendment Effective Date: 2026-03-01. Billing Cutoff Date: 2026-03-01.
  - If change is prospective only: March invoice reflects $110k; no historical adjustments.
  - If back-billed for Feb at new rate and customer approved: Additional invoice for Feb delta = $10k.
